Men Arrested Near UK Air Base Used By US Forces In Iran War
British police have arrested several men on suspicion of explosives offenses near an air base used by US forces, prompting the evacuation of residents from nearby homes.
Police declared a major incident on September 27 near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, western England, and said army bomb-disposal experts were examining several vehicles.
RAF Fairford is used by the US Air Force and has been used for US military operations against Iran.
Several properties in the nearby village of Whelford were evacuated, and residents were taken to a local leisure center, police said.
Armed police were seen blocking access to the main gate of the base, according to Reuters.
In March, Britain granted the United States permission to use RAF Fairford and another British base for what the government described as specific and limited defensive action against Iranian missile facilities. The permission was later extended to missile sites and capabilities threatening shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps warned in July that any base used for strikes against Iran would be considered a legitimate target, according to Reuters.
There was no immediate indication that the arrests were connected to Iran or to any foreign government.
The US Air Force said it remained vigilant and would take appropriate measures to protect US personnel, civilians, contractors, and their families, according to Reuters.
British authorities have also warned in recent months about the threat of hostile activity and possible sabotage by state actors, including Russia. The British government has said it does not comment on specific intelligence or security threats.
Gloucestershire police said it believed the incident was contained.
